label: Formatting
summary: Statement layout, indentation, comments, operators, and region comments.
must_follow: Almost every SSL statement, including comments, must end with a semicolon.
Never include a semicolon inside comment text; the first semicolon ends the comment and the remaining text becomes executable code.
Use spaces around assignment, arithmetic, comparison, and logical operators.
Use /* region / /* endregion comments for editor grouping instead of :REGION / :ENDREGION.
Prefer tabs for indentation; if the file already uses spaces, preserve 4-space indentation.
Comments explain purpose, ownership, safety consequences, replay behavior, or a non-obvious ordering requirement; do not narrate assignments or restate syntax.
In a banner or doc block, describe a failure result or an empty case only when the code produces one; do not add outcomes to fill the template.

elements.name: DECLARE
elements.summary: Declares one or more variables in the current SSL scope.

elements.name: PARAMETERS
elements.summary: Declares named input parameters for a script, procedure, method, or constructor.

elements.name: DEFAULT
elements.summary: Assigns a fallback expression to a parameter when the caller omits that argument.

elements.name: INCLUDE
elements.summary: Inserts another SSL script's source into the current file so its statements compile as if they were written inline.

elements.name: PUBLIC
elements.summary: Declares public variables shared across the running program — reachable from any procedure until the program context clears them.
